value.body: A sports performance analyst uses video and data to help coaches and athletes see what is working. Professional teams, sports academies, leagues and some sports-tech companies hire for this work. A typical day involves filming or reviewing sessions, tagging key moments, and preparing clips and reports for the coaching staff.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BPES / B.P.Ed or B.Sc Sports Science

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Video tagging software, wearable data, spreadsheets

items.label: B.P.Ed. enrolment
items.note: Physical education degree; most graduates teach or coach
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 11 (programme-wise enrolment, all modes, actual responses)

items.label: B.P.E.S. enrolment
items.note: Bachelor of Physical Education and Sports
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 11 (programme-wise enrolment, all modes, actual responses)

items.label: Khelo India recognised academies
items.note: Academies recognised under Khelo India for training athletes

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Many start as video analysts or interns with academies and teams, often after a short performance-analysis course. Strong tactical knowledge of one sport plus comfort with video and spreadsheets is the usual combination.

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: lead analyst, sports scientist, scouting or coaching roles.
Openings are few and concentrated in professional sport.
Travel with teams and match-day hours are common.
